partners.mechanism_chain: MBTPS2 (HGNC:7334) —DISRUPTS→ SREBP processing (GO:0032242); SREBP processing (GO:0032242) —LEADS_TO→ Keratosis follicularis spinulosa decalvans (MONDO:0010637); SREBP processing (GO:0032242) —LEADS_TO→ Collagen biosynthesis (GO:0006407); Collagen biosynthesis (GO:0006407) —LEADS_TO→ Osteogenesis imperfecta, type 19 (MONDO:0049223). Loss-of-function mutations in MBTPS2 disrupt SREBP processing, which is a critical pathway involved in regulating gene expression for lipid and cholesterol metabolism, and importantly, also plays a role in cellular processes that impact collagen biosynthesis. Dysregulation of SREBP processing can indirectly affect collagen production and maturation, leading to phenotypes like osteogenesis imperfecta. Furthermore, the disruption of MBTPS2 function directly impacts epidermal differentiation and keratinization, manifesting as keratosis follicularis spinulosa decalvans.

partners.mechanism_chain: MBTPS2 (HGNC:24109) —DISRUPTS→ ER-associated degradation pathway; MBTPS1 (HGNC:7539) —DISRUPTS→ ER-associated degradation pathway; ER-associated degradation pathway —DECREASES→ ER protein homeostasis; ER protein homeostasis —LEADS_TO→ Keratosis follicularis spinulosa decalvans (MONDO:0010637); ER protein homeostasis —LEADS_TO→ Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, kondo-fu type (MONDO:0032721). Mutations in MBTPS2 cause X-linked keratosis follicularis spinulosa decalvans, while mutations in MBTPS1 cause spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, kondo-fu type. Both genes are critical for the ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathway. Disruption of ERAD by either gene leads to impaired protein homeostasis within the endoplasmic reticulum, ultimately manifesting as the distinct phenotypes of these two diseases.

partners.mechanism_chain: MBTPS2 (HGNC:24088) —DISRUPTS→ SREBP processing (GO:0032057); SREBP processing (GO:0032057) —LEADS_TO→ Keratosis follicularis spinulosa decalvans (MONDO:0010637); SAR1B (HGNC:10088) —DISRUPTS→ COPII vesicle formation (GO:0005893); COPII vesicle formation (GO:0005893) —DISRUPTS→ ER-associated degradation (ERAD) (GO:0030162); ER-associated degradation (ERAD) (GO:0030162) —LEADS_TO→ Chylomicron retention disease (MONDO:0009528). While MBTPS2 and SAR1B are distinct genes, loss-of-function mutations in both lead to disruptions in ER protein processing and trafficking pathways. MBTPS2 dysfunction impairs SREBP processing, contributing to KFSD, while SAR1B dysfunction impairs COPII vesicle formation, a critical step in ER export and a component of the broader ERAD pathway, leading to CRD. Both diseases thus converge on cellular dysfunction related to protein homeostasis within the ER.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that genetic variants in MBTPS2 do not affect UPR signaling or that variants in COL1A1 do not impact Type I collagen synthesis, or if these pathways are found to be completely independent in their regulation and downstream effects. _(variant: rs77124232)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic link between UPR and collagen synthesis in KFSD and OI16 could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both conditions. Modulating UPR signaling or collagen processing pathways might offer a strategy for ameliorating the phenotypic severity of these disorders.
